title: A fixed lunar clock phase from shallow M5.5+ earthquakes in 2000-2012 gave no clear positive transfer in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested whether a common phase at the main lunar semidiurnal frequency persists in global shallow earthquakes. We used a fixed USGS ComCat sample with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth from 0 to 70 km. We learned the phase from 5,628 events in 2000-2012 and tested it on 4,845 events in 2013-2025. The later coefficient along the learned phase was -1.69% of mean phase density. Its conditional 95% year resampling interval was -5.58% to +2.54%. A monthly group phase test gave a two-sided p value of 0.43824. Resampling both halves gave an interval of -5.14% to +3.26%. Weekly and yearly group tests also did not resolve a signal. The pooled amplitude was 0.94%, with monthly phase p = 0.84744. These results give no clear positive phase transfer. They do not show a physical phase reversal or the absence of tidal triggering. A fixed mean lunar clock does not include local ocean response or fault stress. Spatial pooling, event dependence, catalog changes and only 13 years in each half limit the result. The package contains code, aggregate monthly evidence, random draws, a figure, source hashes and repeat instructions. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: The later lunar clock coefficient and its monthly rotation null are shown at left. Conditional year intervals are shown at right. All intervals include zero. The clock is not local tidal stress.
